authorSelfScore.scorer: author self-score (the authoring agent; not the independent score create-rigged-character-assets requires)
gaps: Ruby jewels on the shoulder and thigh bosses are brass caps: the 4-material budget (two shared brass sets, gunmetal, hound-glow) and no vertex colours leave no red material.
Glow reads peach rather than hot orange in the Blender compare at the project's GLOW_STRENGTH 0.7 convention; the grille and side lenses are less luminous than the concept.
Front view: the skull reads narrower and much darker than the concept's broad lit face, and the eye slits are small from the front; the ears read as upturned flaps rather than folded rose ears.

Forelegs are plated cylinders with a gunmetal wrist joint and a short angled pastern; the concept's forearm plate is a more sculpted taper with engraved panels, and its far-side legs are staggered while the model's rest stance is symmetric.
Front view chest is a single smooth bulb with the grille low on the prow; the concept's cuirass carries more plate seams, rivets and engraved panel lines everywhere.
Paws are simpler than the concept's arched, individually jointed toes.
authorSelfScore.method: Author self-score from spring-hound.fidelity-compare.jpg: orthographic Blender renders of the low-poly model at the concept's side, front and back angles, framed at the concept's own metres per pixel (side 1.2 m / 855 px, front/back 1.21 m / 875 px), judged side by side and by 50/50 overlay. Supporting silhouette IoU against background-thresholded masks (difference > 22 from the corner colour, 5 px median): side 0.43, front 0.33, back 0.23. The IoU understates the match: the polished skull and gunmetal parts render near the background tone head-on and drop out of the render mask, and the painted concept's soft shading and far-side legs inflate its mask. The compare lighting is the fixed warden-matched rig and was not tuned to the score.

independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the model)

rubric.note: Side view keeps the long, low body, the coil spine and the key tail, so the outline matches at a glance. The legs are straight stiff tubes without the concept's angled hocks and tapered forearm plates, the head is a long flat crocodile snout instead of the greyhound skull, and head-on the skull is narrow and dark with ears that flare like horns.

Present and readable: the coiled spring spine, the neck coils, the winding key on a segmented tail and the hinged toothed jaw. Weak or missing: the chest grille is unlit bars between two peach side lenses, so the lenses out-read the core. The eye slits are small peach dashes, and the ruby bosses are brass caps. The ruby is a choice, not the budget: the warden and escapement carry jewel colour through COLOR_0 within 4 materials, while the hound spent a slot on a second brass set.

The plates separate cleanly over gunmetal joints. They are smooth, with none of the concept's engraved panel lines, seams or rivets. The hammered normal reads as noise rather than painted wear, and the paws are simplified blocks.

The brass reads saturated orange-copper against the concept's olive gold, the ruby accent is absent, and the glow reads peach and dim (the GLOW_STRENGTH convention is accepted; the failure is that it does not act as a focal light).
The engine shots read clearly as a low brass hound, distinct from the upright roster. The face goes dark head-on and no chest light marks the hit-reaction focal point.

topFixes: Make the chest core the focal light: a bright hound-glow panel behind the grille bars, larger and brighter than the side lenses, plus brighter and longer eye slits.
Restore the ruby bosses through COLOR_0 on a factor material, as the warden's planets and the escapement's sapphires do, or merge the two brass sets to free a material slot.
Reshape the head into a broader, shorter greyhound skull with folded rose ears and a lit face. Give the legs angled hocks and tapered, engraved forearm plates.
independentScore.method: independent visual review against assets-source/concepts/hound-sheet-1.png by a separate reviewer agent. Judged the concept sheet at native resolution against the side, front and back orthographic compare, the owner review sheet, the low 3/4 Blender render and the five in-engine clip shots (seated player, about 2.6 m). Rubric: silhouette and proportions 30, signature features 25, surface detail and material read 20, colour and value 15, readability at play distance in the engine shots 10.
